posts.title: Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below
posts.summary:
Chips are getting bigger, more modular, and much more capable as new innovations mix with existing processes and long-researched projects go mainstream.
The post Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The industry is shifting toward multi-die assemblies and heterogeneous integration as traditional monolithic reticle-sized dies can no longer meet the performance requirements of modern AI workloads.
The rise of agentic AI necessitates a more complex mix of CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators, moving beyond the simple scaling of identical GPU clusters.
Design complexity has reached a point where AI-driven tools are now required to validate architectures, ensuring that chips remain manufacturable and testable within larger heterogeneous systems.

To achieve the target of two orders of magnitude improvement in performance-per-watt, the industry must fundamentally realign its manufacturing processes to prioritize advanced packaging and chiplet-based architectures alongside logic scaling.

posts.title: Kids outlearn AI—and we still don’t know why
posts.summary: People have been talking to each other for at least 100,000 years, as best we can tell. And in all that time, there has been only one thing in the world that could learn a human language to perfect fluency: a human child.  Now there are two.  Four short years after the release of ChatGPT,…
bullets: Current LLMs require roughly 100,000 times more linguistic data than a human child to achieve comparable fluency, highlighting a massive disparity in data efficiency.
Frontier AI models are currently trained on trillions of tokens, but researchers warn that the supply of high-quality, easily available internet data could be exhausted by the 2030s.

The inability of AI to match human learning efficiency is driving a shift in research focus toward reverse-engineering childhood cognitive development to create more sustainable, data-efficient models.
Stanford and Georgetown researchers emphasize that while LLM progress is impressive, the current 'brute force' scaling method is reaching a point of diminishing returns regarding data availability.

bullets: The transition to HBM4 introduces the option for custom base dies, allowing architects to optimize memory for specific XPU workloads rather than relying on standard off-the-shelf components.

posts.title: Overcoming China’s Supply Chain Leverage
posts.summary:
Since joining the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2001, China has, barely without foreign notice, executed one of the most consequential economic strategies in modern history. When it entered the WTO, roughly 33 percent of Chinese exports were intermediate goods, or the components, chemicals, and parts that go into making final products. By 2025, that figure had risen to 46 percent.1 This did not happen by accident. The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) made a deliberate strategic decision to, as it has framed it, make the world dependent on China while making China independent of the world.2 Supply chain supremacy was always intended as a geopolitical weapon.
Continue reading Overcoming China’s Supply Chain Leverage on American Affairs Journal.
bullets: China has strategically increased its share of global intermediate goods exports from 33 percent in 2001 to 46 percent by 2025, creating systemic global dependency.
Beijing has demonstrated a consistent pattern of using market access as a geopolitical weapon, targeting foreign corporations like Lotte to exert pressure on sovereign government decisions.
Corporate boards are increasingly exposed to supply chain coercion, as China’s economic strategy is designed to make the world dependent on its industrial base while insulating its own economy.

posts.title: The Augmentation-Automation Race
posts.summary:
The actual effects of AI on the labor market still seem shrouded in deep uncertainty. When it comes to predictions on near-term impacts, we can see two camps emerge. A deep bench of established and renowned labor economists continues to expect “small” effect sizes, at least by the standards of the drastic predictions common in San Francisco. They predict local disruptions, yes, but expect they’ll be offset by broad-based productivity gains and job growth in other fields. Yet in much of Silicon Valley, a different view prevails. The creators of the technology, most prominently Anthropic’s CEO, Dario Amodei, predict widespread displacement and high unemployment. If there is absorption of the displaced, it will be into worse jobs that might not even be around for long. On that view, AI is markedly abnormal: while past technologies have complemented distinctly human contributions, such as intelligence or creativity, AI is sufficiently broad and general that we should expect it to exceed and supplant these human contributions to the economy, leaving human workers largely obsolete...
Continue reading The Augmentation-Automation Race on American Affairs Journal.
bullets: Labor economists remain divided on AI's impact, with some predicting productivity-driven job growth while others, including industry leaders like Anthropic’s CEO, warn of widespread human obsolescence.
The core debate centers on whether AI will act as a complement to human labor or as a general-purpose technology capable of supplanting human intelligence and creativity entirely.
The uncertainty surrounding AI’s labor market effects poses significant risks for long-term economic planning and workforce development strategies.

posts.title: AI’s recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all
posts.summary: The AI industry’s boldest promise right now is that AI will soon improve itself, with almost no need for human oversight. LLMs can already write code, generate synthetic data for training, and optimize the computer chips they run on. Forecasts of explosive AI progress predict that what researchers call recursive self-improvement is on the horizon. …
bullets: New research from Princeton suggests that current AI agents lack the judgment and creativity required for open-ended, innovative research, challenging the timeline for recursive self-improvement.
While AI models excel at narrow engineering tasks, they struggle with high-level research activities like hypothesis generation and determining when to abandon unproductive lines of inquiry.
The study utilized a 'shadow evaluation' method, testing models like Claude Opus 4.8 against unpublished NeurIPS 2026 papers to measure their ability to perform original scientific work.

The findings indicate that the industry's hype regarding fully automated, self-improving AI research may be premature, as models currently fail to meet the standards of top-tier machine learning conferences.

The transition to 800VDC architectures necessitates the adoption of solid-state transformers to reduce the number of conversion stages and minimize energy losses.

This shift represents a fundamental change in power delivery design, moving from traditional 48V or 12V architectures to high-voltage DC systems to support the massive thermal and efficiency demands of modern AI hardware.

posts.title: Controlling Voltage Droop In 2.5D PIM Chiplet Architectures (Washington St., UW-Madison)
posts.summary:
Researchers from Washington State University and University of Wisconsin–Madison published a technical paper titled “ReVolt: Power Delivery Network-Aware Voltage Droop Control for 2.5D PIM Chiplet Architectures.” Abstract “Processing-in-memory (PIM)-based 2.5D multi-chiplet platforms are enablers for machine learning (ML) workloads. However, their performance is affected by the power delivery network (PDN), where varying chiplet-level current demand... » read more
The post Controlling Voltage Droop In 2.5D PIM Chiplet Architectures (Washington St., UW-Madison) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers have developed 'ReVolt,' a framework designed to mitigate voltage droop in 2.5D Processing-in-Memory (PIM) chiplet architectures used for ML workloads.
The system utilizes an LSTM-based surrogate model to predict per-chiplet voltage trajectories, allowing for proactive adjustments to operation unit (OU) sizes.
By dynamically controlling current demand, the ReVolt framework prevents voltage violations and improves the energy-delay product (EDP) by an average of 76x compared to existing baselines.
The solution maintains high ML inference accuracy while addressing the critical performance degradation caused by power delivery network (PDN) instabilities in multi-chiplet systems.

posts.title: How the “censorship-industrial complex” is changing the internet and US policy
posts.summary: I first heard the term “censorship-industrial complex” on April 15, 2025.  That’s when I got the tip that a small office in the U.S. State Department, which focused on monitoring and countering foreign disinformation from the likes of Russia, Iran, and China, was facing imminent shutdown—the next day.  And the reason? R/FIMI, as the office…
bullets: The 'censorship-industrial complex' narrative has transitioned from fringe online discourse to a central pillar of the second Trump administration's domestic and foreign policy.
The concept led to the shutdown of the State Department's R/FIMI office, which was previously tasked with countering foreign disinformation from Russia, Iran, and China.
This policy shift carries significant implications for global internet governance, as it challenges the collaborative frameworks between government and tech platforms used to moderate online content.
The narrative is supported by a network of well-funded conservative media and nonprofits, fundamentally altering how information policy is debated and implemented in the US.

posts.title: Ambitious American Science Requires Reliable and Effective Federal Funding
posts.summary: IFP’s comments on OMB’s proposed rule on Federal Financial Assistance
bullets: The OMB has proposed a rule granting the government authority to terminate discretionary grants at any time and requiring political appointees to conduct pre-issuance reviews for all awards.

Critics argue that these changes will destabilize federal funding, as the threat of arbitrary termination undermines the long-term planning necessary for critical sectors like energy, infrastructure, and R&D.
Mandating political oversight over expert merit reviews threatens to degrade the quality of scientific research by prioritizing political alignment over technical feasibility.
The proposed rule risks increasing the administrative burden on grantees and reducing the overall credibility of federal financial assistance programs.

posts.title: Building a practical path to post-quantum cryptography
posts.summary: Quantum computing has alternated between breakthrough darling and overhyped promise in technology circles. Its powerful new capabilities come with a threat to break current cryptography, but for business leaders navigating the noise, the signal should be clear: post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is a manageable evolution, not a crisis. The mathematics behind today’s encrypted digital transactions may…
bullets: Experts estimate a 50-50 probability that quantum computers will be capable of breaking 2048-bit RSA encryption by 2040, necessitating a long-term strategic shift in cybersecurity.
Enterprises are advised to prioritize protection against 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks, where sensitive data is intercepted today for future decryption by quantum-capable adversaries.
The transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is framed as a manageable, phased evolution rather than an immediate crisis, allowing firms to modernize infrastructure without systemic disruption.

Data centers are gearing up for a future in which a single rack could consume as much power as an entire building.

Hyperscalers already are collaborating to establish standards for 1-megawatt racks, and as AI workloads grow more continuous, autonomous, and power-intensive, there is an ongoing debate about whether developing...
Technologies like optics, specialized silicon, and high-voltage DC systems can enable a more fragmented future with distributed workloads and reduced density.

Scale-up has typically been defined as a single rack with copper interconnect, with programmers using memory semantics.
That definition is getting fuzzier.

posts.title: 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec)
posts.summary:
Researchers from imec published a technical paper titled “Are Gate-All-Around 2D CFETs the Optimal Architecture for the A2 Node and Beyond?” Abstract Excerpt: “Here, we develop an A2-oriented 2D CFET integration flow with a CPP of 36 nm and Lg of 10 nm and present initial demonstrations of several key process modules. Despite their atomically... » read more
The post 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Imec research indicates that 2D Gate-All-Around (GAA) CFETs do not offer a contacted poly pitch (CPP) scaling advantage over traditional Silicon GAA CFETs at the A2 node.
The study highlights that contact formation constraints impose a minimum CPP of 36nm, necessitating rigorous co-optimization of contacts and parasitics.
The team utilized a multiscale power-performance-area (PPA) evaluation framework, incorporating quantum transport simulations and circuit-level benchmarking to assess the viability of 2D materials.

These findings suggest that while 2D materials are promising, their integration into A2-node architectures requires significant process module innovation to overcome current physical scaling limitations.

posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced the industry's first 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, enabling DSP-less host-to-module connectivity.
Transitioning to linear optics can reduce module power consumption by up to 50%, significantly lowering thermal loads in high-density AI data center racks.
The solution eliminates the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers, providing a scalable path toward 224G/448G interconnects and Co-Packaged Optics (CPO).
By meeting or exceeding CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 specifications for jitter and eye-closure, this IP provides a standardized, interoperable foundation for next-generation AI infrastructure.

posts.title: Self-Supervised Layout Generation To Fix Advanced-Node DRVs (Nvidia, Duke)
posts.summary:
Researchers from NVIDIA and Duke University published a technical paper titled “SCALE: Self-Supervised Constraint-Aware Layout GEneration for Local P&R DRV Fixing at Advanced Nodes.” Abstract “As semiconductor manufacturing advances toward sub-2nm nodes, local place-and-route (P&R) design-rule violation (DRV) fixing is increasingly limited by complex rule interactions, dense multi-layer routing geometries, and foundry-specific constraints. While Large... » read more
The post Self-Supervised Layout Generation To Fix Advanced-Node DRVs (Nvidia, Duke) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from NVIDIA and Duke University developed SCALE, a self-supervised framework designed to automate the fixing of design-rule violations (DRVs) at sub-2nm nodes.
The framework utilizes a domain-adapted Vision-Language Model (VLM) that learns to reconstruct masked layout polygons, providing geometric guidance for complex routing issues.
SCALE improves the solve rates of existing automated agents by 12% to 25%, achieving up to 97% success on real-world sub-2nm layout cases.
By automating the repair of spacing, width, and color-spacing violations, this technology addresses the growing bottleneck of manual layout fixing in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

posts.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
posts.summary: Business and technology leaders need no convincing that the time of agentic AI is here. Organizations are rapidly adopting agents, and few executives doubt the technology’s potential to transform work. But many organizations find that realizing the desired return on investment (ROI) from AI hinges on having the right foundation, with inadequate infrastructure and data…
bullets: A survey of 300 executives reveals that legacy data infrastructure is the primary bottleneck preventing the effective scaling of autonomous AI agents.
Current enterprise AI agents have access to an average of only 45% of company data, while top-performing 'data leaders' ensure access to over 70%.
Gartner predicts that AI agents will automate or augment 50% of business decisions by 2027, making the modernization of data access systems a critical priority for ROI.
Successful deployment of agentic AI requires moving beyond simple question-answering systems to providing agents with real-time, frictionless access to structured and unstructured operational data.
